_comment: 🧩️ AVI 1.0/✳️any's own contribution to the repository test platform — its mutation oracle registration and its declared mutation vocabulary (wave 7, ticket 26/08/23/END-TO-END-TESTING-REFACTOR). No standalone Rust crate reads AND writes AVI credibly (`avirus` 0.2.5 never parses a typed header and its 'write' path copies the whole hdrl section byte-for-byte; `rff-format-avi` 0.1.0's own doc comment says its muxer is 'still scaffolded'; `oxideav-avi` 0.0.9 has real depth but zero independent adoption — created 2026-04-19, 0 GitHub stars/forks, would pull in an equally unvalidated `oxideav-core`). AVI IS a RIFF container, so the reference here composes `riff` 2.0 — a mature, independent, heavily used (11.9M downloads) generic RIFF/LIST/chunk reader/writer, MIT, unrelated to this repository — with a hand-written AVI 1.0 hdrl/strl/movi/idx1 codec against the format's own public byte layout. Same composition shape ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🗿️artifacts/💬️bcf's oracle already established for zip+quick-xml, for the identical reason: no standalone crate exists for the specific format, so two independent, credible, more-generic layers are composed instead of adopting a weaker/unlicensed substitute. Full investigation and evidence: .🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️23/END-TO-END-TESTING-REFACTOR/📓️w7-avi-1-0-mutate-report.md. Discovered by convention alongside ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio's own top-level manifest; merged into one registry, no central edit required.

oracles.rationale: What `riff` provides: the generic RIFF layer only — chunk id/size framing, LIST nesting with a 4-byte type tag, even-byte padding, all read AND written through `riff::Chunk`/`riff::ChunkContents` (not this subset's own `🚪️io/🦀️component.rs`, which hand-rolls the same primitives independently). What this module provides on top: AVI 1.0's OWN semantics against the format's public specification — `avih`/`strh`/`strf` (BITMAPINFOHEADER/WAVEFORMATEX) field layouts, the movi-fourcc-to-stream-index numbering convention, and the idx1 AVIIF_KEYFRAME/offset convention — none of which `riff` knows anything about. This is the same composition shape ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🗿️artifacts/💬️bcf's oracle already established for zip+quick-xml (no standalone BCF crate exists either): two independent, credible, more-generic reference libraries composed over the real format's own documented shape, rather than a single weaker or unvalidated format-specific crate. Genuinely differential: this composition both decodes AND re-encodes every one of the 13 declared AviMutation kinds through riff's own chunk writer, never by echoing input bytes.

comparisonProfiles.description: AVI 1.0 documents compared structurally: the main header's 10 typed DWORD fields plus dwReserved, idx1Present, and every stream IN ORDER (stream index is semantic identity in AVI — the movi fourcc's own leading 2-digit stream number — unlike a guid-keyed document; there is no natural stable identity for a stream or a movi chunk beyond its position). Each stream's strh (all 16 fields) and strf (BitmapInfo/WaveFormat/Raw, discriminated by a `format` tag) project as their full typed structure; each movi chunk projects as fourcc, keyframe flag, and a size+digest of its payload rather than raw bytes, since a real chunk in the committed fixture runs into the tens of kilobytes — the same opaque-binary-payload treatment the fleet brief's own raster/mp4 precedent gives large payloads. Every top-level unknown chunk (an unrecognised chunk or LIST directly inside the RIFF form, tagged `LIST:<type>` for the latter) projects the same way, in file order. Arrays are order-significant throughout: streams, chunks and unknown chunks are all positional in this format, never set-like.
